gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Anker's store says the Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus cannot use its 240V output while it is charging from 120V AC, so a 240V well pump fed from that station stops whenever the owner recharges it from a 120V wall outlet or a 120V-only generator during an outage. Anker sells a separate $399.99 240V Bypass Charging Cable for charging and powering at the same time.
standout_why: I compared against offgridbenchmark.com, holdbackup.com and thewell.guide. offgridbenchmark has the most on power stations. It checks the F3800 (not the Plus) on paper and gives a 9,000 W surge, says the F3800 Plus surge is not listed, and works out runtime. It does not mention the 240V lockout during 120V charging or the 25 A cap on the L14-30R port. holdbackup only links to a separate power-station guide. thewell.guide covers generators, the PB30 inlet, L14-30 cords and interlocks, and says only that a battery system that can start a 240V pump often costs $5,000 or more. None of the three says how to keep a 240V pump running while a battery station recharges. That decides whether the bypass cable and a 240V-output recharge generator belong in the Anker cart.
kit_items: Battery with 240V output: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus (3,840 Wh LFP, L14-30R 120/240V port, 25 A and 6,000 W max). It is one of the few single units on approved stores that puts out 240V for a 230V submersible pump.

Way into the house: Anker SOLIX Smart Home Power Kit (Smart Home Panel + subpanel + breaker + ground bar, sold bundled with the F3800 Plus), or the Pro/Tran 2 50 A 10-circuit 120/240V manual transfer switch, which Anker lists for the F3800 Plus. The switch has one 30 A 2-pole and one 20 A 2-pole slot, so it can hold the pump's double-pole circuit. It is UL 1008, and Anker says an electrician installs it.

Recharge path that keeps the pump on: Anker SOLIX 240V Bypass Charging Cable ($399.99), plus a 240V-output gas generator or a 240V wall outlet. Without the cable, charging from 120V AC turns off the 240V output.

Alternative set: BLUETTI Apex 300 + B300K + Home Backup Kit (single Apex 300). BLUETTI says it powers 120V and 240V devices at the same time and rates it 3,840 W. Its 7,680 W figure is 'Lifting Power', which BLUETTI's own blog describes as a mode for resistive loads, not motors, so it is not a pump-start rating.

Not in any cart: the pump's nameplate data (HP, 2-wire or 3-wire, LRA) and a licensed electrician. Franklin's LRA figures, as quoted by offgridbenchmark, are 23 A for a 1/2 HP 3-wire motor and 41.8 A for a 1 HP 3-wire motor at 230V, against the F3800 Plus port's stated 25 A max. Anker publishes no surge figure for the F3800 Plus.
